# Results — Study 362 (Piotroski F-Score)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Joseph Piotroski's **9-point
F-Score** — the fundamental-health checklist said to "separate winners from losers" — rebuilt
from **EDGAR companyfacts** for a fixed basket of large/mid-cap US firms and tested as a
cross-sectional **high-minus-low** portfolio held the following calendar year. Forward returns
from **yfinance** daily adjusted closes. The synthetic positive control is offline & deterministic;
run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Fundamentals | EDGAR companyfacts (`data.sec.gov`, public, no key) — annual 10-K figures |
| Prices | yfinance daily adjusted closes → calendar-year **total** returns |
| As-of | **2026-06-22** (the in-progress **2026** calendar year is dropped before stats) |
| Basket | 40 large/mid-cap tickers; **21** survive the all-9-concepts intersection (see caveat) |
| Panel | fiscal years **2009 → 2024** → returns **2010 → 2025**; **249** firm-years scored |
| F-score mean | **5.54** / 9 (distribution spans 1 … 9) |
| Portfolio | long F-score **≥ 7**, short **≤ 4**; fiscal year *y* → calendar-year *y+1* returns |
| Lag / costs | 1-calendar-year reporting lag; **10 bps** one-way × 2 legs (round-trip each) + **50 bps** borrow on the short |
| Fingerprints | F-score `5334c548fb8a` · returns `cd16bc81edd3` |

> **Survivorship + small-basket caveat (named on the Signal axis).** The basket is a fixed set
> of firms that *survived* to 2026, pulled on current tickers — a mild **upward** tilt (the dead
> losers a low F-score would have flagged are missing). And because the F-score needs all nine
> raw inputs, only **21** firms (≈16/year) clear every concept — financials & utilities drop out
> for lack of a clean COGS/gross-margin line. With ~16 names a year the canonical **8-9 vs 0-1**
> split is too thin to populate (the bottom tail is near-empty), so we use **≥7 vs ≤4**; the
> verdict does not hinge on the exact cut (see the threshold sweep). Treat every real-tape number
> as an **upper bound** on the live effect.

## The signal — high-minus-low F-score portfolio (fiscal *y* → returns *y+1*)

| leg | mean annual return | note |
|---|--:|---|
| high F-score (**≥ 7**) | **+14.77%** | the "winners" |
| low F-score (**≤ 4**) | **+12.13%** | the "losers" |
| equal-weight basket | **+16.37%** | the honest benchmark |
| **high − low spread** | **+2.64%** | the advertised edge |
| **high − market** | **−1.60%** | the "winners" trail the basket (HAC *t* = **−1.38**) |

| metric | value |
|---|--:|
| usable years | **15** |
| spread mean | **+2.64%/yr** |
| spread volatility | 14.6% |
| spread Sharpe | 0.18 |
| spread win-rate | **53%** (8 / 15 years) |
| **Newey-West (HAC) *t* of the spread** | **+0.62** |
| **placebo *p*** (random same-size portfolios) | **0.256** |

Read it carefully. The high-minus-low spread is **positive** — fundamentals *look* like they
sort. But (a) at **HAC *t* = 0.62 / placebo *p* = 0.26** it is **statistically indistinguishable
from random stock-picking**; (b) the spread is driven entirely by the *short* leg — the
high-F-score "winners" earn **+14.8%/yr** versus **+16.4%/yr** for the equal-weight basket, so the
celebrated winners *trail the market* (high − market = **−1.6%/yr**, *t* = −1.38). The F-score
mostly *avoids a thin tail of losers*; it does not pick winners on this tape.

## It isn't monotone — the very top bucket underperforms the middle

Mean next-year return pooled across years, by F-score bucket:

| F-score bucket | mean next-year return | firm-years |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0–1 | **+3.2%** | 3 |
| 2–3 | +10.7% | 25 |
| 4–5 | +17.4% | 87 |
| 6–7 | **+17.4%** | 110 |
| 8–9 | **+15.7%** | 24 |

Return rises with the score up to the **6–7** bucket and then **falls** at **8–9**. A genuine
"separate winners from losers" factor climbs monotonically to the top; here the very-best firms
do *worse* than the merely-good — exactly the noise you'd expect when the top bucket holds a
couple dozen firm-years.

## Costs + borrow finish it off

| | gross | net @ 10 bps × 2 legs + 50 bps borrow |
|---|--:|--:|
| spread mean | +2.64%/yr | **+1.74%/yr** |
| HAC *t* | +0.62 | **+0.41** |

The annual long-short rebalance pays a round-trip on each leg plus borrow on the short; that
~0.9%/yr drag pushes an already-insignificant spread further down. Net *t* = 0.41 — there is no
deployable edge to charge against.

## Robustness — the threshold doesn't rescue it

| split (hi ≥ / lo ≤) | usable years | spread | HAC *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 8 / 3 | 2 | −4.6% | −0.28 | 0.61 |
| 7 / 3 | 8 | −1.4% | −0.57 | 0.61 |
| **7 / 4** (headline) | **15** | **+2.6%** | **+0.62** | **0.26** |
| 6 / 4 | 15 | +4.5% | +1.06 | 0.11 |
| 6 / 5 | 15 | +0.9% | +0.50 | 0.38 |

The spread flips sign and *t* wanders with the cut; the best case (6 / 4) still only reaches
*t* = 1.06. There is **no threshold on this basket where the F-score spread clears *t* = 2.**

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, the tape is honest

Deterministic firm × year panel where a latent quality drives both the 9 binary points and (via
`planted_edge`) next-year returns. The detector + inference must recover a planted edge and must
**not** manufacture significance when there is none:

| planted edge | usable years | high leg | low leg | spread | HAC *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (null) | 18 | +10.7% | +9.9% | **+0.86%** | **+0.75** | 0.252 |
| **0.04** | 18 | +16.5% | +6.5% | +10.03% | **+8.61** | 0.000 |
| **0.10** (large) | 18 | +25.2% | +1.4% | +23.79% | **+19.91** | 0.000 |

With **no** planted edge the test stays at *t* = 0.75 (no false positive); a real edge of 4%/yr
already drives *t* past 8. The machinery is unbiased — so the real-tape *t* of **0.62** is exactly
what an **absent or tiny** edge looks like through this keyhole, not a power failure.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The high-minus-low spread is positive (**+2.64%/yr**) but at HAC
  **t = 0.62 / placebo p = 0.26** it cannot be told apart from random portfolios; it is
  **non-monotone** (the 8–9 bucket trails 6–7), it **flips sign** across thresholds, and the
  high-F-score leg **underperforms the equal-weight basket**. Decades of academic support (the
  effect is real and stronger among small, illiquid, low-analyst-coverage value stocks) plus a
  sub-2 *t* on *this* large-cap, survivorship-tilted tape ⇒ **WEAK**, not REAL. A synthetic
  control proves the engine, never the market.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net of one-way costs × turnover + borrow the spread is **+1.74%/yr**
  at *t* = 0.41 — inside the noise, and built on a long leg that lags the market. On the universe
  where Piotroski's edge is *documented* (micro-cap, hard-to-borrow value names) the borrow and
  impact are *worse*, not better. Not a NAV-scale strategy here.
- **Winners vs losers? — BUSTED.** On this tape the high-score "winners" don't beat the market;
  the score mostly *sidesteps a thin tail of losers* and is non-monotone at the top. The
  9-point checklist is a sensible *quality screen*, not the winner-picking machine the headline
  sells — the separating power lives in a universe (and an era) this large-cap survivor basket
  isn't.
